output.title: `pac package deploy` hangs indefinitely (deadlock) deploying X++/FnO external package
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a UDE-linked F&O environment via Power Platform Admin Center (no LCS project).

Build an X++ model with custom table/field extensions in Visual Studio 2022 (Unified Developer Experience tooling). Confirm the model deploys successfully via Extensions → Dynamics 365 → Deploy → Deploy Models to Online Environment in Visual Studio (this path works correctly and is not affected by this bug).

Create a Dataverse 'Package Deployer' project (pac package init) and add the X++ deployable package as an external package: pac package add-external-package --package-type xpp --path <deployable-package.zip>.
Build the project (dotnet build) to produce the package DLL and PkgAssets/ImportConfig.xml.

Ensure the referenced zip is a correctly-formed Power Platform Unified Package (containing fnomoduledefinition.json at the root plus the compiled model folder) — produced via the official Azure Pipelines XppCreatePackage@3 task with CreateCloudPackage: true.
Authenticate: pac auth create --environment <env-url>
Run: pac package deploy --package <path-to-package.dll> --logConsole --verbose
output.actual_result: the main thread blocks forever on an internal ManualResetEventSlim.Wait() inside pac's own deployment code, waiting for a signal that is never sent

output.title: Power Apps CLI package bug with complex object parameters
steps_to_reproduce: Generate a Power Apps Code Apps connector service for any Dataverse OData function that accepts a complex or object-typed parameter.
Call the generated service with a valid object value.
Observe that the request fails with error `0x80060888`, regardless of the object supplied.
output.expected_result: Complex or object-typed parameters should be serialized as bare JSON object literals using `JSON.stringify(value)`, similar to how arrays are currently handled.
output.actual_result: Objects are converted using `String(value)`, which produces: `[object Object]`. This results in malformed OData parameter serialization and causes the Dataverse request to fail.

output.title: `pac env fetch` inconsistent output
steps_to_reproduce: Create an XML file (environment-variables.xml) with the following FetchXML query: <fetch version='1.0' output-format='xml-platform' mapping='logical' distinct='true'><entity name='environmentvariabledefinition'><attribute name='schemaname' /><attribute name='defaultvalue' /><link-entity name='environmentvariablevalue' from='environmentvariabledefinitionid' to='environmentvariabledefinitionid' link-type='outer' alias='env'><attribute name='value' /></link-entity></entity></fetch>
Execute the `fetch` command while referencing the XML file created in step 1: pac env fetch --xmlFile environment-variables.xml
Re-execute the command from step 2.
Note the columns and values that were output.
output.expected_result: Results returned should respect the FetchXML query specified (column order and sorting).
output.actual_result: Subsequent executions of the same `pac env fetch` command results in different outputs. Sometimes, the columns / values are output as: schemaname defaultvalue ... Other times, it's output as: schemaname env.value ...

output.title: Duplicate Quick Create form definitions in solution packing
steps_to_reproduce: Create a solution, add a table and create a new Quick Create form
Add an 'onLoad' event handler to the new Quick Create form
Use the Power Platform source control integration to commit the solution to git
Clone/download to git repository
Navigate to the solution root folder and run `pac solution pack --folder ./ --zipfile QuickCreateForm.zip --packageType managed` to generate an example.zip solution file
Attempt to import the example.zip managed solution file into another environment.
Manually unzip the QuickCreateForm.zip solution file and view the customizations.xml file.
output.expected_result: When packing YAML solution source, Quick Create form definitions should go under `<forms type='quickCreate'>` only.
output.actual_result: The resulting solution.zip file duplicates the Quick Create form definition under `<forms type='quick'>` as well as `<forms type='quickCreate'>`. This causes solution imports to fail when the quick create form contains an `<events />` definition.
